title: intent-aware-routing-studio-workflow
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build an end-to-end Console experience called 'Routing Studio' that lets customers author, validate, preview, and rollback intent-aware routing policies. Key capabilities: region selection, tier-based routing, and model-variant fallback chains with simulation and canary previews. The feature targets production customers using Dedicated and Private deployments who need deterministic routing behavior across regions and cost/latency tiers.
goals: Expose region selectors in policy composer with region affinity and hard/soft constraints
Add tier routing rules (e.g., premium/standard/cheap) with weight and capacity hints
Support fallback chains by model variant (quantized/ensemble/cheaper models) with automated compatibility validation
Provide a preview/simulator mode that runs synthetic traffic against routing rules and shows expected route distribution, latency and cost estimates
Enable canary rollouts and instant rollback from preview to live policies
acceptance_criteria: Console policy composer can create and save policies that include region selectors, tier routing, and fallback chains
Validation step flags incompatible fallbacks (e.g., incompatible model architecture or missing region availability) with actionable messages
Preview mode simulates 1k synthetic requests and shows per-route token-cost and p50/p95 latency projections
Admin can promote a preview policy to live and initiate a canary at 1% traffic and later rollback with historical diff
E2E tests cover region routing logic across three regions and two tiers and assert deterministic fallback ordering

progress_updates: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: scoped feature to focus on region affinity, tier weights, and fallback by variant. Linked PRD: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RST/Intent-Aware+Routing+Studio

2026-03-03 - Design review: PM and Design aligned on single-pane composer with 'stages' for primary and fallback rules. Feedback: prefer explicit compatibility check for model families. Design doc: https://drive.redwood.com/designs/routing-studio-v1

2026-03-08 - Engineering sync: agreed schema for policy bundle (flat rule list + precedence). Backend implemented validation endpoint /api/v1/policies/validate (stub). GitHub issue tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/412

2026-03-12 - Prototype demo: UX prototype wired to validation endpoint; initial simulator runs but cost estimates are over-pessimistic — decision to integrate runtime telemetry for better unit cost modeling. Recorded demo: https://meet.redwood.com/recordings/2026-03-12-routing-studio-proto
design_feedback: Prefer showing region availability heatmap next to selector (Design suggestion from Lina Martinez)
Add an 'override' toggle for enterprise admins to force a specific region for compliance-bound customers
Clarify fallback ordering visually and allow drag-and-drop reorder in composer
engineering_notes: Validation service will check: region availability table, model-variant compatibility matrix, and quantization support per device family
Simulator will reuse the existing traffic-simulator microservice but needs extensions for cost/latency modeling based on historical SLO telemetry
Plan to expose a 'policy-diff' endpoint used by Rollouts to compute safe rollback points
Potential perf risk: simulator running 1k synthetic trials per preview could spike the routing runtime — will sandbox on dedicated infra
open_questions: Should the policy composer surface suggested fallback variants automatically based on model cost/latency profiles, or leave it fully manual?
What is the canonical source of truth for region availability — infra inventory or model catalog?
How to represent multi-region stickiness for sessions that must preserve KV cache locality?
tradeoffs: Automatic suggestion of fallback variants improves time-to-setup but may surface non-obvious regressions in quality; decided to include suggestions with an explicit 'quality risk' badge
Running close-to-production simulator yields more accurate estimates but increases infra cost — compromise: run a lightweight simulator by default and a heavy simulator on-demand
Storing full historical previews for rollback increases storage; we will store diffs and the policy bundle only
risks: Incorrect fallback compatibility checks could route traffic to a model that produces invalid structured output
Preview cost/latency estimates diverge from production if telemetry window is insufficient
Enterprise compliance customers may require hard region constraints that conflict with autoscaling policies
qa_plan: Unit tests for validation rules and compatibility matrix
Integration tests running preview simulator with canned workloads across three regions
Manual exploratory QA with tenant A/B testing and canary promotion/rollback scenarios
Load test to ensure preview simulator does not degrade live routing SLOs
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal feature flag for Redwood employees and a small set of dogfood customers
Phase 2: Soft launch to 5 enterprise customers (opt-in) with 1% traffic canary capability
Phase 3: General availability with doc guide and sample policy templates
Rollback: Provide single-click rollback to previous live policy and automated alerting on increased error rate
notes: Customer ask: a fintech customer requested region-hardening for GDPR-sensitive flows — prioritized as part of template set
Follow-up task: productize policy templates for common patterns (latency-first, cost-first, compliance-first)
Action item: schedule security review if KMS-protected telemetry is used for cost modeling
